answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy binds every identity to a verifiable proof-of-work trail. Each new account must solve a memory-hard puzzle whose difficulty shifts like a dune, rising automatically with network demand. The solution leaves a cryptographic echo that older peers co-sign before it becomes a vertex in a global trust graph. Spawning ten thousand fake identities therefore burns ten thousand times the compute, and no single echo can be reused, so the attacker cost grows linearly while an honest agent pays once.
